intended_object: The canonical coprojection of the summand F(X₁ i₁, X₂ i₂, X₃ i₃) into the coproduct ∐_{p(i₁,i₂,i₃)=j} F(X₁ i₁, X₂ i₂, X₃ i₃). That coproduct is the degree-j component of the graded object obtained by applying the trifunctor F to graded objects X₁, X₂, X₃ and regrading along p. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The body is just `ιMapObj` from Mathlib's general API, applied to the triply graded object `(i₁,i₂,i₃) ↦ F(X₁ i₁)(X₂ i₂)(X₃ i₃)` at the index ⟨i₁,i₂,i₃⟩. `ιMapObj` is the coproduct inclusion into `mapObj`, the fiberwise coproduct over p⁻¹(j). So this is exactly the inclusion of the (i₁,i₂,i₃) summand into the degree-j component of `mapTrifunctorMapObj F p X₁ X₂ X₃`, as the docstring says. It works for arbitrary categories, index types and maps p, with only the coproducts assumed to exist (`HasMap`). That is the natural generality, so nothing is too narrow. It is a convenience specialization of `ιMapObj`, and it is mathematically correct.
